newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian bourse seeks foreign trading links.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian bourse seeks foreign trading links.

text.p: The Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange is seeking to link its scripless trading and settlement system with foreign depositories in a move to encourage foreign interest, a local newspaper said on Monday.
"We won't embark on it until we have completed transferring warrants and loan stocks into the CDS," KLSE executive chairman Nik Mohamed Din was quoted as saying in the Star newspaper.
The CDS is the exchange's Central Depository System, which eliminates physical clearing of trades, allowing brokers to offer a more efficient service.

Linking the CDS with foreign depositories would make it easier for foreign investors to buy Malaysian shares as the investors would not be required to register with the CDS but only with their own respective depositories, the article said.

Malaysian stocks have already been transferred into the computerised CDS system, and the transfer of warrants and loan stocks into the CDS is expected to be completed by the third quarter of this year.

Nik Din said the KLSE had not officially begun any talks with foreign depositories. "For the foreign depositories, they want to evaluate how successful our depository system is," he said. -- Kuala Lumpur newsroom (603 230 8911)
